lesson_title: Eggs in an Egg Box: Why Volume Division Lies
hook_text: Crate volume ÷ can volume = the WRONG answer. Every time. Here's the count that works.
clip_script: Fitting cans into a crate is the egg-box problem. Nobody pours eggs into a box and hopes; the box has spots. Cans of diameter 6 in a crate 30 long: five spots. Across the 24 width: four. The floor is a grid of 5 by 4 — 20 spots. Crate 12 high, can 12 tall: one storey. Twenty cans. Never divide volumes — the clever-sounding shortcut overcounts, because cans are round and crates are square: the corners around every can are dead air that liquid maths would happily fill. And if the crate were 32 long? Still 5 cans — the spare 2 centimetres holds nothing. Fitting rounds DOWN. Count spots, not space.
visual_style: Top-down crate grid filling with cans one row at a time, corner gaps flashing red as a ghostly 'volume answer' can tries to squeeze in and bounces out.
pacing: Rhythmic row-by-row fill, one comic rejection beat, crisp rule stated at the end.
